basis: Abnormal bone formation or resorption defines this skeletal disease umbrella.
Congenital glomerular protein loss and progressive renal damage; secondary lipid abnormalities and delayed tooth eruption do not establish other organ damage.
Inherited chylomicron metabolism disorder; pancreatitis and hepatic steatosis are separately diagnosed complications; lipemia retinalis does not impair vision.
Neuralgia involving cranial nerves defines a peripheral nervous system disorder.
Porencephaly and cerebellar malformations define the syndrome; cardiac defects and corneal clouding are reported without established frequency.
Inherited optic atrophy with mitochondrial metabolic dysfunction; extraocular neurologic disease is variable and not established in most across this umbrella.
Carcinoma originates in the parotid salivary gland, which belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.
Cutaneous melanoma arising in eyelid skin; both eyelid and skin are defining sites.
A psychiatric behavioral disorder without defined damage to an organ axis.
Malignant B-cell lymphoma warrants blood-cell and lymphoma mechanism axes; its breast site has no anatomical axis.
Craniosynostosis, limb abnormalities, ptosis and strabismus define the syndrome; hearing impairment and intellectual disability occur in fewer than 30%.
Short-rib skeletal dysplasia; associated pulmonary hypoplasia impairs respiration commonly (~30%+). Common intrinsic renal damage is not established for IFT80 disease.
The definition specifies mild microcytic anemia from HBA2 variation; severe thalassemia complications should not be extrapolated.
Accelerated myeloid leukemia directly affects marrow and blood cells; splenic involvement is within the same axis.
Severe short-rib dysplasia; lethal pulmonary hypoplasia is typical and brain defects are described as common (~30%+). Renal and biliary lesions lack common frequencies.
Primary cutaneous B-cell lymphoma directly occupies skin and is a malignant lymphocyte disorder.
Intellectual disability and cardiac malformations define the syndrome; skeletal abnormalities occur in 3/3 assessed and strabismus in 2/3. Four-axis cap reached.
Postpartum psychiatric psychosis; neither its obstetric setting nor associated confusion establishes direct organ damage.
Limb reduction defects and cardiac anomalies define the syndrome; respiratory insufficiency in 30-79% does not establish direct pulmonary pathology.
Glycosylation disorder defined by neurologic dysfunction and hypogammaglobulinemia; hepatic injury is not established as common, and cardiopulmonary findings are occasional.
Uterine disease is outside the axes; inflammation alone does not establish infection or autoimmunity. The discordant pyelonephritis child does not define this concept.
Maxillary sinus collapse and progressive enophthalmos are defining structural abnormalities of the sinus and orbit.
Respiratory-chain metabolic defect; neurologic dysfunction includes hypertonia in 3/5. Respiratory failure in 2/5 lacks proven lung injury; optic pallor has limited sampling.
Intestinal loss of function caused by defective neural control defines the condition, directly linking bowel dysfunction and its innervation.
Parkinsonism caused by cerebrovascular pathology; brain dysfunction and its defining vascular disease support both axes.
